name: navigator-no-unguarded-main-git
body:
The distributed `codebase-navigator` must have no raw git grant that can rewrite the main checkout's branch refs or move its HEAD/working tree, and so bypasses the verify gate. Integration of a change-set into main happens ONLY through `apg project merge <name>` (verify gate → merge → main rebuild → self-clean).

Today (verified) the template's frontmatter `bash:` block (`opencode-suite/agents/codebase-navigator.md` lines 71-76) grants `git merge *`, `git checkout *`, `git switch *`, `git rebase *`, a blanket `git worktree *`, and a blanket `git branch *`. The blanket `git branch *` is NOT read-only: `git branch -f main <sha>` force-moves main's branch ref past the verify gate, and `git branch -D` / `git branch -m` delete or rename refs. A grant the spec calls read-only must not admit those forms.

Required grant set (per verb):
- REMOVE `git merge *` — merging into main is `apg project merge`'s job, behind the verify gate.
- REMOVE `git checkout *` and `git switch *` — they move the main checkout's HEAD/working tree; the flow never needs them (the project branch lives in its worktree; `apg project start` creates it).
- NARROW `git worktree *` to read-only listing (`git worktree list *`) — worktree add/remove is owned by `apg project start` / `apg project merge`'s self-clean.
- NARROW the blanket `git branch *` to the exact, genuinely read-only pattern `git branch --show-current` (it prints the checked-out branch and takes no ref-writing option). The blanket `git branch *` is removed because it admits ref-writing forms — `git branch -f <branch> <sha>`, `git branch -D`, `git branch -m`. Branch listing is deliberately not granted: it is unnecessary (the branch/worktree identity comes from `apg project start`'s printed path and `git status`), and narrowing to the single exact inspection pattern removes the ref-rewrite risk entirely. No grant the spec calls read-only may admit rewriting a branch ref.
- KEEP `git rebase *` — the agent-builder main-flow step "rebase the project worktree onto main" needs it; the template must state it is run with cwd INSIDE the project worktree (rebasing the project branch onto main), never in the main checkout.
- KEEP read-only `git status *`, `git diff *`, `git log *` — with one caveat: `git diff *` and `git log *` admit the output-redirect option `--output=<file>`, which writes an arbitrary file (including inside the main checkout). `--output=<file>` is FORBIDDEN on every granted git verb; the navigator runs `git diff` and `git log` to stdout only. This is a prose-enforced known risk (the glob cannot exclude the form), recorded in `requirements.constraint.main-integration-via-merge-gate-only` alongside the worktree-only `git rebase` rule.

Acceptance criteria:
- The navigator template's frontmatter `bash:` block grants none of `git merge`, `git checkout`, `git switch`, a blanket `git branch`, or unrestricted `git worktree`; the read-only git patterns it grants are exactly `git status *`, `git diff *`, `git log *`, `git branch --show-current`, and `git worktree list *`, plus `git rebase *` for the worktree-only sync.
- The navigator never passes `--output=<file>` (or any output-redirecting option) to a granted git verb; `git diff`/`git log` output goes to stdout only, and `requirements.constraint.main-integration-via-merge-gate-only` states this forbidden form and records it as a known risk exactly as it does for the worktree-only `git rebase` rule.
- Its body states that main is integrated only via `apg project merge`, and that `git rebase` is run only inside the project worktree for the agent-builder sync step.
- `AGENTS.md` states the same (its "Worktree isolation" section no longer calls a blanket `git branch` a read-only verb).
- Scope: `opencode-suite/agents/codebase-navigator.md`, `AGENTS.md`; the repo's own `.opencode/agents/**` are NOT edited.
